caseStudy.title: AtlasLedger
caseStudy.background:
AtlasLedger provides a high-volume, tenant-scoped document assistant. A Container Apps HTTP gateway dispatches durable work to Service Bus. An AKS retrieval API queries Azure Database for PostgreSQL with pgvector. Stable and canary deployments run side by side during a traffic migration. During a recent retry storm, some jobs committed a result before their message locks expired but were delivered again before final acknowledgment.

The access policy forbids unfiltered chunks from entering generation. The model index must stay versioned during a migration, and query filtering is mandatory regardless of recall loss. The PostgreSQL connection budget is shared by both deployments. Operators want to compare p95 request duration by revision and distinguish delay from dependency calls.

The SRE team requires that canary rollback preserve both the tested stable image and its retrieval configuration. No rollout may cause active pods to exceed the available database connection budget.

exhibits.title: Rollout and connection budget
exhibits.code:
Database limit: 240
Reserved outside retrieval: 48
Stable max replicas: 8
Canary max replicas: 4
Same pool maximum per replica on both revisions

exhibits.title: Relevant AKS manifest
exhibits.code:
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 2
    maxUnavailable: 0
# Assume at most one deployment rolls at a time.

exhibits.title: PostgreSQL retrieval (SQL)
exhibits.code:
SELECT doc_id, content FROM chunks
WHERE tenant_id = $2 AND generation = $3
ORDER BY embedding <=> $1
LIMIT 20;
::

questions.prompt: What shared per-replica pool maximum respects the budget during the specified rollout surge?
questions.explanation: 240 minus 48 leaves 192. Up to 8 + 4 + 2 = 14 replicas can coexist. Floor(192/14) is 13.

questions.prompt: A scheduler requires 650m CPU and 1 GiB memory per new Pod. Node A has 900m CPU and 768 MiB free; node B has 500m CPU and 2 GiB free. How many additional Pods fit without changing requests or adding nodes?
questions.explanation: The scheduler fits both resource requests on the same node. A fails memory and B fails CPU, even though the sums look sufficient.

questions.prompt: The meridian change feed processor is being scaled to 11 instances with a shared processor identity. Which state enables partition ownership and checkpointing?
questions.answer: The lease container shared by these processor instances
questions.explanation: A shared lease container coordinates assignment and preserves progress across instances.
options: The lease container shared by these processor instances
The cluster node hostname in each document
A separate new lease container per instance
The vector query continuation token reused as a lock

questions.prompt: Order the retrieval path for the meridian assistant after the caller submits a query. Resolve scope before contacting the data tier.
answer: Determine the verified tenant and retrieval generation
Embed the question using the selected generation encoder
Retrieve up to 15 nearest eligible rows with metadata predicates
Supply only eligible chunks and their provenance to generation
questions.explanation: The retrieval scope must be established before retrieving data, and the query vector must match the index.

questions.prompt: The meridian Cosmos transport gets HTTP 429. What minimum timing should its first custom retry honor before retrying?
questions.answer: Wait at least 1500 ms as indicated by the service

Retry only after changing the consistency level
Wait at least 1500 ms as indicated by the service
Retry immediately on another client

Complete the broker delivery

questions.prompt: The Azure Managed Redis cache for meridian stores per-tenant answers. Which cache key is sufficient when changing model generations?
questions.answer: meridian:<verified-tenant>:<model-generation>:<query-hash>
questions.explanation: Tenant scope and model generation are both retrieval inputs and must participate in cache identity.
options: meridian:<model-generation>:<query-hash>
meridian:<verified-tenant>:<model-generation>:<query-hash>
meridian:<query-hash>
meridian:<verified-tenant>:<query-hash>

questions.prompt: An AKS worker receives storage errors after rotating its managed identity's federated credential. Its current service account is worker in namespace rag, but the federation was created for namespace default. What exact correction preserves the identity boundary?
questions.answer: Set the federated subject to system:serviceaccount:rag:worker for the intended issuer and audience
questions.explanation: The projected token subject must match the federated credential, including both namespace and service account.
options: Install the resource owner’s API key in all namespaces
Add an Azure role assignment but leave the mismatched subject
Set the subject to the node pool name
Set the federated subject to system:serviceaccount:rag:worker for the intended issuer and audience

observed subject: system:serviceaccount:rag:worker
federated subject: system:serviceaccount:default:worker

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL canary changes the query encoder and index generation behind App Configuration. Some clients refresh while stale replicas continue serving. What invariant prevents cross-generation search and stale-cache reuse?
questions.answer: Read one generation per request and use that generation for both the encoder/index pair and the tenant-scoped cache key
questions.explanation: A request-scoped generation couples compatible retrieval components and cache identity through an overlapping migration.
options: Read one generation per request and use that generation for both the encoder/index pair and the tenant-scoped cache key
Read the current encoder setting and previous index setting independently and reuse cache entries globally
Send the same vector to all generations and prefer whichever returns first
Disable the metadata filter for rare cross-generation cache misses

questions.prompt: The meridian Docker image builder installs dependencies again after every application-only edit. Which Dockerfile edit fixes that without bundling build tools?
questions.answer: Copy dependency metadata before application code and install the dependencies in a build stage
questions.explanation: Docker invalidates layers downstream of a changed COPY. Separate stable dependency inputs and use a runtime stage for the output.
options: Copy dependency metadata before application code and install the dependencies in a build stage
Move the application COPY below CMD but keep it before dependency installation
Install build tools in the final stage at process startup
Copy the entire repository before dependency installation

WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN pip wheel -r requirements.txt -w /wheels

Always overwrite with the most recently delivered event
Only apply an event whose version is strictly newer than the stored document version

client.list_properties_of_secrets()
client.get_secret("meridian-db-password")
